name: VY Sgr
description: A Cepheid in the Milky Way that pulsates every 13.56 days; its mean radius is 98 solar radii.

radius.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, VY Sgr: Baade-Wesselink mean radius (solar radii) 98 +/- 5.2 (Monte-Carlo)

temperature.source: Groenewegen (2020), A&A 635, A33, VizieR J/A+A/635/A33/table1, recno 255, Name='VY Sgr', columns Teff, e_Teff (K): Teff 4250 +/- 189 K from a fit to the spectral energy distribution at mean light (not spectroscopic)

distance.source: Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10, VY Sgr: Baade-Wesselink distance (pc) 2702 +/- 143.9 (Monte-Carlo)

color.reason: Interstellar dust reddens every spectrum of this star, E(B-V) = 1.283 +/- 0.077 (Groenewegen (2013), A&A 550, A70, table10), and its light changes through each pulsation

text.card: A Cepheid in the Milky Way, 98 times the Sun's width, that swells and shrinks every 13.6 days.
text.introduction: Its mean radius, 98 solar radii, comes from comparing how fast its surface moves with how its size changes, 2,702 parsecs away.
text.locator: table10, VY Sgr: Per, Rad, Dist

notes: The star pulsates; it is drawn at its mean radius.
No dynamical mass is measured for this Cepheid; its mass is left unmeasured.
